findings.title: Row items are off by a few pixels
findings.evidence: span#lovable-badge-text “Edit with” and span#lovable-badge-logo sit in the same row but their top edges differ by 2px (870 vs 868). 1px is sub-pixel noise; 2–3px is a mistake, not a decision.
findings.fix: Align them on the same axis: use align-items on the parent, or give both the same margin-top. If the offset is intentional, make it ≥ 8px so it reads as deliberate.

findings.title: 11 pulsing status dots
findings.evidence: Small round elements animating with “float-slow”. The blinking green dot that says “live” / “available” is on every AI-generated landing page.
findings.fix: If something is actually live, show the live thing (a number, a timestamp). Otherwise remove the dot.

findings.title: Gradient-filled text (1)
findings.evidence: span.text-gradient “focus deeper.” uses background-clip: text with a gradient. Decorative, hurts contrast, and reads as generated.
findings.fix: Use a solid colour. Emphasis comes from size and weight, not a rainbow.

findings.title: Headline could be on any site in the category
findings.evidence: h1: “Study smarter, focus deeper.”. No product name, no number, no specific noun. 21st.dev's five-minute test: cover the logo; if the copy still works for a competitor, it isn't yours.
findings.fix: Write one specific claim: what it is, for whom, and the one thing it does that others don't. Specific beats clever.
findings.citation: 21st.dev: generic copy is the strongest tell

findings.title: Inter for 86% of the text
findings.evidence: Primary family is Inter, one of the fonts generated UIs default to. Fonts seen: Poppins, Inter, system-ui.
findings.fix: Not wrong on its own. If everything else is default too, this is the cheapest thing to change: pick one typeface with a point of view for headings and keep the workhorse for body.
findings.citation: Impeccable overused-font; HN thread on vibe-coded tells (Inter everywhere)

findings.title: 1 row of three identical cards
findings.evidence: Three 355px-wide cards of equal weight (“"FocusFlow turned my stu”, “"The rainy café scene + ”, “"Finally, a single tool ”). The hero + three feature cards skeleton is tell #9; equal weight tells the reader nothing is more important than anything else.
findings.fix: Decide which one matters and make it bigger, or turn the three into one sentence each under a single heading. Break the symmetry once.
findings.citation: vibecoded-design-tells #9; 21st.dev: uniform features is a top-5 tell

findings.title: 71 elements animating at rest
findings.evidence: Keyframes in use: twinkle, float-slow, pulse. Motion on everything is tell #4.
findings.fix: Animate the one thing you want the eye to go to. Everything else should hold still.

findings.title: Centered hero: big headline, centered sub, centered buttons
findings.evidence: h1 at 72px, centered, with 4 centered blocks under it. On 23.5% of Show HN launches. It's the layout every builder emits when nobody chooses one.
findings.fix: Not a problem on its own, but combined with other tells it's the skeleton. Left-align and put the product next to the headline, or lead with the product itself.

findings.title: Blurred colour blobs behind the content (2)
findings.evidence: div.absolute.inset-0 is a blur(40px) wash. The aurora backdrop is the default "atmosphere" of generated heroes.
findings.fix: Remove it and let the content carry the first screen. If you want atmosphere, use one real image.

findings.title: 4 em dashes in 1.6k characters
findings.evidence: 2.5 per 1,000 characters. Humans use them; generated copy uses them in nearly every paragraph, and readers have learned to notice.
findings.fix: Keep the ones that do work; turn the rest into commas, periods, or parentheses.
findings.citation: Impeccable em-dash-overuse; Slopdar em-dash signal; HN thread

findings.title: Head is missing: canonical, favicon
findings.evidence: No JSON-LD structured data either, so AI search engines have nothing to cite. One h1, good.
findings.fix: Ten minutes of <head> work: title under 60 chars, canonical URL, lang attribute, favicon, and an Organization or WebSite JSON-LD block.
